steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Moon orbits the Earth every 27.3 days (sidereal period), but the lunar phase cycle (synodic period) is 29.5 days because the Earth-Moon system also orbits the Sun.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The phases in order: new moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent, new moon.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Moon phases are caused by the changing angle between the Earth, Moon, and Sun, which determines how much of the Moon's illuminated hemisphere we see from Earth.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Moon always shows the same face to Earth (tidal locking / synchronous rotation): its rotation period equals its orbital period.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Why is the synodic period (29.5 days) longer than the sidereal period (27.3 days)? | Q: Name the eight phases of the Moon in order. | Q: Why does the Moon always show the same face to Earth?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Because the Earth-Moon system moves around the Sun during the Moon's orbit. After one sidereal orbit, the Moon must travel an extra ~27° to catch up with the Sun's new position, adding about 2.2 days. | New moon, waxing crescent, first quarter, waxing gibbous, full moon, waning gibbous, last quarter, waning crescent. | Tidal locking (synchronous rotation): the Moon's rotation period equals its orbital period (both 27.3 days). Earth's tidal forces slowed the Moon's rotation until it became locked.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Learn the 8 phases in order — drawing a diagram with the Sun, Earth, and Moon positions for each phase is the best way to remember. The 5° orbital tilt is the key to explaining why eclipses don't happen monthly — always mention this. For lunar eclipse questions, explain the red colour via atmospheric refraction/scattering of red light. Know the difference between sidereal period (relative to stars) and synodic period (relative to Sun) and WHY they differ.
